issues.legal_issue: A purchaser at a revenue sale of separately notified shares does not acquire the rights of a purchaser of the entire estate merely because the shares together comprise the whole estate.
material_facts: Separate accounts were maintained for the two shares comprising the estate, and the arrears due from each share were listed separately.
The sale notification described the shares as separate units and did not state that the entire estate was being sold.
The separate demands were not merged, and no fresh notification for sale of the entire estate was issued.
Although both shares were sold at the same sale and together comprised the whole estate, the purchaser claimed the right to annul under-tenures as purchaser of the entire estate.
issues.conclusion: The sale was of the separate shares, not of the entire estate as such, and the purchaser did not acquire the privilege of annulling under-tenures conferred on a purchaser of the entire estate.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 6, 13, 14 and 37 of the Bengal Land Revenue Sales Act, 1859, the section 6 notification is conclusive as to whether the subject of sale is the entire estate or separate shares. Where separate accounts exist, a sale of the entire estate requires closing or merging those accounts into one demand and issuing a fresh notification for the entire estate; only a purchaser of the entire estate obtains the section 37 privilege. The judgment notes earlier consistent decisions in Satish Chandra Hui v. Sudhir Krishna Ghosh, Gunendranath Mitra v. Bimal Kumar Hui, and Gowranga Sundar v. Rakhal Majhi.

rule.if: revenue_sale_proceeding and separate_accounts and separate_arrears_listed and notification_identifies_shares and shares_together_comprise_estate and not whole_estate_sale_procedure_completed

predicates.revenue_sale_proceeding: A public sale is conducted to recover revenue arrears from an estate or its shares.
predicates.separate_accounts: The estate's shares are recorded and accounted for separately.
predicates.separate_arrears_listed: The arrears attributable to the separate shares are stated separately for the sale.
predicates.notification_identifies_shares: The sale notice identifies the separate shares, rather than the estate as a whole, as the property offered for sale.
predicates.shares_together_comprise_estate: The shares offered separately together make up the whole estate.
predicates.whole_estate_sale_procedure_completed: The separate accounts are closed or merged into one demand and a notice is issued offering the entire estate for sale.

issues.definition: When a revenue sale concerns separately accounted shares that together comprise an estate, and the notice offers the shares separately without the steps for an entire-estate sale, the purchaser cannot annul under-tenures as an entire-estate purchaser.

issues.legal_issue: A collector may sell separately accounted defaulting shares even when every share is in default, while a sale of the entire estate requires the prescribed procedure for that sale.
material_facts: The estate was divided into separately accounted shares, and arrears were due from both shares.
The collector notified the separate shares for sale and stated the arrears due from each separately.
The purchaser argued that separate-share sale was unavailable because no share was free from default.
issues.conclusion: The collector was authorized to notify and sell the defaulting shares separately even though all shares were in default; the sale could not thereby be treated as a sale of the entire estate.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 13 and 14 of the Bengal Land Revenue Sales Act, 1859, protect separately accounted shares and permit the defaulting shares to be sold as such; section 13 does not require a non-defaulting share. If the collector proposes to sell the entire estate, the separate accounts must first be closed or merged into one demand and a fresh section 6 notification issued. No earlier case is relied on as the doctrinal basis for this statutory interpretation.

rule.if: revenue_sale_proceeding and separate_accounts and all_shares_in_default and separate_arrears_identified

predicates.revenue_sale_proceeding: A public sale is conducted to recover revenue arrears from an estate or its shares.
predicates.separate_accounts: The estate's shares are recorded and accounted for separately.
predicates.all_shares_in_default: Revenue arrears are due from every separately accounted share.
predicates.separate_arrears_identified: The arrears due from the separate shares are identified individually.

issues.definition: When a revenue sale concerns separately accounted shares and each share is in default with its arrears separately identified, the collector may sell the defaulting shares separately.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser's acceptance of rent from occupants as tenants may support an inference that their lands were resettled with them, even without a specific pleading of resettlement when the underlying facts were pleaded and the purchaser was not prejudiced.
material_facts: The occupants alleged facts showing that they possessed the lands and paid rent to the purchaser of the tenure.
The purchaser accepted those payments while treating the occupants as tenants.
The underlying facts supporting resettlement were pleaded, although resettlement was not specifically pleaded as a separate case.
The occupants established their claims only as to the lands for which they proved their entitlement.
issues.conclusion: Resettlement could be inferred from the acceptance of rent and treatment of the occupants as tenants; the lack of a specific pleading did not prejudice the purchaser, and the claims were rightly decreed to the extent proved.
issues.legal_principle: A court may infer resettlement from conduct showing that a purchaser treated occupants as tenants and accepted rent from them. A failure specifically to plead resettlement does not defeat that inference where the facts supporting it were pleaded and the opposing party was not prejudiced. The judgment mentions section 22 of the Bengal Tenancy Act in relation to the earlier merger and transfer of occupancy rights, but its resettlement conclusion rests on the parties' conduct; no earlier case is relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: tenancy_or_land_claim_proceeding and rent_paid_by_occupants and rent_accepted_as_tenant_payment and underlying_conduct_facts_pleaded and no_prejudice_from_specific_pleading_omission

predicates.tenancy_or_land_claim_proceeding: A proceeding concerns occupants' claimed rights in land following a transfer of a superior tenure.
predicates.rent_paid_by_occupants: The occupants pay rent for the land to the person holding the superior tenure.
predicates.rent_accepted_as_tenant_payment: The recipient accepts the rent while treating the occupants as tenants.
predicates.underlying_conduct_facts_pleaded: The facts about possession, rent payment, and its acceptance are pleaded.
predicates.no_prejudice_from_specific_pleading_omis: The absence of a separate, specific assertion of resettlement does not impair the opposing party's ability to meet the case.

issues.definition: In a land-rights proceeding, where occupants pay rent and it is accepted as tenant rent, the supporting conduct is pleaded, and omitting a specific assertion of resettlement causes no prejudice, resettlement may be inferred.
